headline: 9% of subscribers may churn, risking PKR 2.76 M this month
paragraphs: We scored 100,000 paying subscribers and expect about 9,076 (9%) to cancel in the next 30 days, putting PKR 2,764,263 of monthly revenue at risk, with the top 10,000 (top 10%) accounting for PKR 1,012,831 of that risk [F1,F2,F3,F4]

The leading reasons among the high‑risk group are ‘Followed title just ended’ (content) for 76%, ‘Watching much less than last week’ (viewing) for 42%, ‘Negative support ticket’ (support) for 34%, ‘Failed renewals’ (payment) for 24% and ‘Low balance at renewal’ (payment) for 23% [F5,F6,F7,F8,F9]

Key segments show concentrated risk: 6,644 high‑risk fans out of 29,505 sports followers (T20 International Series) [F10]; 986 high‑risk fans out of 14,121 drama followers (season finale) [F11]; 625 high‑risk fans out of 3,025 kids followers [F12]; the Payment‑troubled group has 5,794 high‑risk subscribers with PKR 1,179,439 at risk [F13]; the Frustrated‑by‑quality group has 2,435 high‑risk subscribers with PKR 662,465 at risk [F14]; the riskiest plan is Sports Premium (12% churn risk, PKR 824,338 at risk) [F15]; the riskiest payment channel is Operator 1 (10% churn risk, PKR 887,853 at risk) [F16]
actions: Send a personalized re‑engagement email to the 6,644 high‑risk sports fans highlighting the upcoming National Cup release in 24 days to encourage continued viewing [F10]
Contact the 5,794 high‑risk subscribers in the Payment‑troubled group to resolve billing issues and protect PKR 1,179,439 of revenue at risk [F13]
Prioritize outreach to the top 10% scored subscribers, as this yields 33% real leavers and is 3.61× more effective than random contact [F1,F4,F17]
